verdict.note: Real Chromium on a throwaway spex dashboard gateway (isolated SPEXCODE_HOME, prebuilt dist): the card's row reads "memory envelope / unknown: missing" on a host that simply has no cap — a mechanism's absence rendered as a defect. The CLI half agrees and is worse: spex doctor --host printed "memory: unknown missing" BOTH uncapped and from inside a systemd-run scope whose cgroup really sets MemoryMax=8G, because detection read fixed paths (/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max, the v1 limit_in_bytes) that no ordinary cgroup-v2 host has. A real cap was therefore undetectable. [[host-facts]]

The launcher clause fails: the pre-fix card carries 9 standing launcher rows on the cross-project panel, every one project-qualified (hi-8bb0/claude-glm: resolves, hi-8bb0/codex: resolves · codex --yolo, …) — one project's .spec/spexcode.local.json rendered as a host fact, which is what the human reported as out of place. The runtime/node/tmux/git/agent-login rows do match the CLI field for field. Measured in real Chromium against a throwaway spex dashboard gateway serving the prebuilt dist. [[host-facts]]

Both halves measured through the real product. Card, in real Chromium against a throwaway spex dashboard gateway serving the dist built at this commit: the row is labelled "memory cap" and reads "cgroup · no cap set" — no mechanism name followed by missing, and no "unknown". CLI: `spex doctor --host` prints "memory cap: cgroup: no cap set" uncapped, and "memory cap: cgroup: 8.0 GiB" from inside systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=8G — the same scope where the pre-fix fixed-path read said "memory: unknown missing". Detection resolved /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/cron.service/memory.max, the cgroup that actually binds this process. [[host-facts]]

The card's three standing rows (toolchain, agent CLIs, memory cap) equal the CLI's field for field: node v24.15.0, tmux 3.4, git 2.43.0, the four agent rows, and "cgroup · no cap set" against the CLI's "cgroup: no cap set". launcherBlockPresent is false and launcherRows is 0 — no project-qualified row on the cross-project panel. Per-project launcher resolution is still named by `spex doctor --host` and by the card's own host-doctor result block, which POST /host/doctor returns carrying the full launchers listing (hi-8bb0/codex: resolves …). [[host-facts]]

spex dashboard on an isolated SPEXCODE_HOME published ~/.spexcode/host.json only after its bind: {version:1, url http://127.0.0.1:5401, pid 3102201, instanceId 0ebe8b1e…, startedAt}. readHostRecord returned that record while the gateway was live. After kill -9 the file is STILL on disk (a killed gateway cannot run dropOwnHostRecord) and readHostRecord returns null — the reader reports no gateway rather than the dead url, which is the whole point of validating the live pid. Re-measured because this node's governed file changed in this branch. [[host-facts]]

Both halves measured in real Chromium against a throwaway gateway on an isolated SPEXCODE_HOME. FAILING CASE (PATH hides git, so the backend genuinely cannot start): the project's own row went from 'start' to 'start / backend for <root> did not come online within 45s — see <SPEXCODE_HOME>/projects/<id>/serve.log see host facts'; serve.log names the real reason (Error: git executable not found on PATH). Exactly one .host-facts-card on the page, zero .host-facts-launchers, and the only host affordance inside the row is the single 'see host facts' link — no second diagnosis UI. TMUX-ONLY CASE: with just tmux hidden, GET /host reports tmux null and host process-host, the backend CAME ONLINE, and the row's action became 'open' — so tmux absence is not a serve failure, which is why the old expectation (a serve failure naming tmux) was measuring behavior this product no longer has and was rewritten in this commit. [[host-facts]]

verdict.note:
Measured on four surfaces at once. The host card in a real headless Chromium (isolated gateway on a throwaway
SPEXCODE_HOME so the live gateway was untouched) carries exactly two labelled rows — `toolchain` and
`agent CLIs` — and its whole innerText is "Host facts / native linux / run host doctor / toolchain / node
v24.15.0 / tmux tmux 3.4 / git git version 2.43.0 / agent CLIs / …": no memory row, and a regex for
memory|内存|cgroup|wslconfig|envelope over the card AND over the entire page body returns false. `spex doctor
--host` in a terminal prints eleven fact lines plus the launcher listing with no match for
memory|cgroup|cap|envelope. `GET /host`'s payload has no `memory` key — grepping the raw JSON for
memory|cgroup|wslconfig|cap yields nothing.

The half that makes this a removal rather than a lucky read: the CLI ran a second time inside
`systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=8G`, and that scope's own memory.max really was 8589934592, so a cap
reader would have had something true to report. It reported nothing. The absence is silence, not a missing
value.

`spex session resources` in the same shell still answers the different question this product does render —
host memory 8313.8/31576.2 MiB, attributed PSS per session, one row flagged orphan:owner-record-absent —
which is [[host-resource-budget]] reading /proc about the sessions that exist, not about a limit the host sets.
[[host-facts]]

Re-measured because the previous pass's own text cited a memory row that no longer exists. The card's facts
still equal the CLI's field for field: runtime `native linux` = `runtime: native linux`; node v24.15.0; tmux
tmux 3.4; git git version 2.43.0; and the four agent rows (claude installed/not logged in, codex
installed/logged in, opencode installed/not logged in, pi installed/logged in) against the CLI's identical
four lines. The card now has TWO standing rows, `toolchain` and `agent CLIs` — the memory row is gone with
its mechanism, so this scenario no longer reads three.

Launcher rows appear on neither standing row: `.host-facts-launchers` is absent from the DOM. To prove that is
suppression of a real fact rather than an empty listing, a deliberately broken launcher
(`broken-eval` → /nonexistent/eval-probe-binary) was seeded in this host's config for the run. `spex doctor
--host` named it `hi-8bb0/broken-eval: BROKEN — /nonexistent/eval-probe-binary --x`, and pressing the card's
own "run host doctor" returned `host doctor: exit 0 — succeeded` with that same BROKEN line inside the result
block — the diagnosis is on demand, never a project-qualified row on the cross-project panel. The seeded
launcher was removed afterwards; the tree is unchanged. [[host-facts]]

Re-measured because host-facts.ts changed when the memory envelope was removed.

Under an isolated SPEXCODE_HOME, `spex dashboard --port 5211` published
{version:1, url:"http://127.0.0.1:5211", pid:549936, instanceId:"c78e205e…", startedAt:…} and readHostRecord
resolved it to a live gateway at that url. The record's pid was the live listener, not the wrapper.

Then kill -9 on exactly the pid the record names — no clean stop, so dropOwnHostRecord never ran and the file
was LEFT on disk. The same reader now says "no gateway": the live-PID check rejects it. A killed dashboard
therefore degrades to absent, never to a wrong url, which is the whole point of validating the record rather
than trusting the file. Port 5211 was free again afterwards.

Re-measured because this node's code: (host-facts.ts) and this scenario's related: (ProjectsPage.jsx) both moved
when the memory envelope left the card — so "exactly one host card and no second diagnosis UI" had to be
re-proven on the card as it now renders.

Real headless Chromium, throwaway gateway under an isolated SPEXCODE_HOME, one offline scratch project. The live
host gateway was untouched (still 401 on :9443 afterwards) and each throwaway was stopped by port.

FAILING CASE, git hidden from PATH: the card names the cause as a host fact (`git missing` beside node and tmux),
and after pressing start the project's OWN row carries the reason and its serve.log —
"backend for /tmp/spex-sf-proj did not come online within 45s — see …/serve.log see host facts" — with exactly
one element matching /host fact/i on the whole page, and exactly one host card before and after. The only doctor
action on the page is the card's own "run host doctor", so no second diagnosis UI appeared. No memory word
anywhere.

NOT A FAILING CASE, only tmux hidden: the card says `tmux missing` with git present, the press settled in 2
seconds, and the row's action became **open** — process-host hosting took over and the backend came online.
Zero "see host facts" links, because there is no failure to link. A missing tmux is a capability change, not a
serve failure.
